en.value: Which of the following is NOT a tragedy?

Rather, it is a satiric comedy in which Plautus presents an amusing setting of human follies and vices. This purpose is to expose and ridicule what is grossly wrong and laughable. Your heart beats around 60 times a minute, delivering nutrients and removing waste from every cell in your body. The nerves that relay input about our required heart rate connect to a specialised centre in the wall of the right atrium (one of the heart's four chambers), known as the sinoatrial (SA) node. Acquired dysfunction is more common, often caused by age, certain medications and lifestyle factors such as increased BMI, diabetes and hypertension. Many people who have a dysfunction may not have symptoms. One of the most common symptoms of a dysfunctional (SA) node, experienced by about two million people a year in the UK, is arrhythmia. This is where the heart beats too fast, too slow or irregularly. There are a variety of treatment options for arrhythmia including cardoversion, pacemakers and cardiac ablation.
